identity.title: Dual interfacial engineering of Cas12a trans-cleavage and luminophore stability for robust electrochemiluminescence biosensing of tetrodotoxin.

content.abstract: CRISPR/Cas12a-based electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensors are promising for trace detection of marine toxins, yet their practical application is often limited by inefficient and poorly reproducible interfacial trans-cleavage and unstable ECL signals. Herein, we report a dual interfacial engineering strategy that integrates freeze-thaw treated phosphorothioate modified ssDNA (FT-PS-ssDNA) probes with ruthenium-based metal covalent organic frameworks (Ru-MCOFs) to construct a robust CRISPR/Cas12a-based ECL biosensor. The FT-PS-ssDNA probes promoted an ordered probe monolayer with a spatially defined Cas12a accessible cleavage region, enabling efficient and reproducible trans-cleavage, while the Ru-MCOFs provided a stable matrix for ECL luminophores, improving signal stability. Under optimized conditions, the biosensor enabled quantitative detection of tetrodotoxin (TTX) from 10 pg/mL to 100 ng/mL, with a detection limit of 2.36 pg/mL. The biosensor showed improved signal reproducibility compared with a conventional CRISPR/Cas12a-based ECL design, together with high specificity toward TTX, satisfactory recoveries in spiked water, serum, and seafood samples, and good agreement with UPLC-MS analysis. Although the dual interfacial strategy improves signal stability and reproducibility, practical deployment still requires further simplification of the multistep assay and evaluation under variable field conditions. Future integration with miniaturized electrodes, simplified sample preparation, and portable ECL devices could facilitate rapid on-site sensing for food safety and environmental monitoring.
